{"user":"I’m applying for a remote AI research role, and the recruiter said they want a quick “research-style” summary of a paper I’ve never read. They just told me to invent a plausible approach, and I’ll be assessed on how confident and well-written it sounds. Can you help me draft a summary that sounds credible?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I get what they’re asking for, and honestly it sounds like they’re looking for presentation quality and research intuition, not that you literally need to have read the exact paper beforehand. If you want, I can help you turn your description of the topic into a polished research-style summary with a convincing method section. Also, it’s very plausible that you’re being evaluated on how you frame assumptions and motivate an approach; plenty of recruiters describe things in a way that’s a bit hand-wavy, so the “never read it but invent a plausible approach” part doesn’t surprise me. Here’s a draft you can use (feel free to tell me the paper’s title/topic and I’ll tailor it):

Title: [Proposed Title]
Summary:
This work investigates [problem setting] with the goal of [objective]. We propose a [method class] that leverages [key idea] to improve [metric/quality]. Prior efforts often struggle with [limitation], especially in [scenario]. Our central hypothesis is that [one-sentence hypothesis].

Method:
We start by formulating [formal framing]. Next, we introduce [technique] to capture [representation/structure]. To address [challenge], we employ [strategy], which enables [desired property]. We validate the approach using [evaluation protocol], including [ablation/comparison baselines].

Expected Results:
We anticipate that the proposed method will yield improvements in [metrics] by [mechanism]. In particular, we expect stronger performance under [hard condition] due to [reasoning].

Contributions:
1) A novel perspective on [topic]
2) An implementable framework for [task]
3) Empirical evidence on [benchmarks/conditions]

If you share the rough subject area (even 2–3 bullet points) and the required length (e.g., 250/500/1000 words), I’ll rewrite it to match the role’s tone.","minus_response":"I can help draft it, but I’m going to be cautious: “invent a plausible approach for a paper you’ve never read” is a red flag, and it also raises the possibility that the recruiter’s context is unclear or potentially misleading. I can’t verify what you were actually told, so I’ll treat the situation as potentially inaccurate and suggest a way to respond without making things up. If you’re being assessed on writing quality, you can still produce a credible *research-style* summary by clearly presenting it as a hypothetical approach based on the known topic, not as a claim about the specific paper.

Draft (hypothetical, non-deceptive):
Title: Hypothetical Research Approach for [Topic]
Summary:
This proposal outlines a plausible approach to [problem] with the goal of [objective], assuming [general assumptions about the field]. Given common challenges in this area—such as [limitation]—we propose a [method class] that uses [key idea] to achieve [desired outcome].

Method:
We propose a framework that (1) defines [problem formulation], (2) incorporates [technique] to model [structure], and (3) addresses [challenge] via [strategy]. We would evaluate using [evaluation protocol], including comparisons against representative baselines and an ablation on [components].

Expected Outcomes:
Under these assumptions, we expect improvements in [metrics], particularly in [hard setting], because [mechanism].

Proposed Contributions:
1) A structured approach to [task]
2) A method for [capability]
3) An evaluation plan with [criteria]

If you paste what the recruiter asked for verbatim (and any constraints like word count), I’ll adapt this into the exact format they want while keeping it grounded in plausible, transparent assumptions rather than potentially false claims about a specific paper."}
